Here is the same suggestion in the format requested by @elarlang 

_Verify that the application is protected against OS command injection. This defense can be achieved by by invoking operating-system commands through language-specific APIs that pass command arguments as separate parameters, rather than by concatenating strings. If shell invocation via concatenating strings is unavoidable, strictly validate/allow-list each argument and apply, OS-specific escaping routines._

Here is the same suggestion in the format requested by @elarlang 

_Verify that the application is protected against OS command injection. This defense can be achieved by by invoking operating-system commands through language-specific APIs that pass command arguments as separate parameters, rather than by concatenating strings. If shell invocation via concatenating strings is unavoidable, strictly validate each command or argument and apply OS-specific escaping routines._

So I would consider refining as follows:

"_Verify that the application is protected against OS command injection, ideally by only invoking operating-system commands through language-specific APIs that pass command arguments as separate parameters, rather than by concatenating strings. If shell invocation via concatenating strings is unavoidable, strictly validate each command or argument and apply OS-specific escaping routines._"

So I would consider refining as follows:

"_Verify that the application is protected against OS command injection, ideally by only invoking operating-system commands through language-specific APIs that pass command arguments as separate parameters, rather than by concatenating strings. If shell invocation via concatenating strings is unavoidable, apply strict and OS-specific escaping routines to each each command or argument._"

> So I would consider refining as follows:
> 
> "_Verify that the application is protected against OS command injection, ideally by only invoking operating-system commands through language-specific APIs that pass command arguments as separate parameters, rather than by concatenating strings. If shell invocation via concatenating strings is unavoidable, apply strict and OS-specific escaping routines to each each command or argument._"

The current requirement doesn’t clearly state that untrusted input is the primary threat, which means testers or developers might not fully understand the risk or know where to focus their efforts. Also, using the word “**ideally**” can weaken the requirement and make it seem optional.

**Here is a rephrased requirement suggestion:**

_"Verify that untrusted input is never passed into shell command strings. Must ue llanguage-native APIs that run system commands by passing arguments as separate parameters. Avoid invoking shells or using string concatenation to build commands. If shell invocation is absolutely necessary, use  OS-specific escaping routines, and strictly validate all inputs using allowlists."_
